? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 12:12:15 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.00 (model confidence 0.87)
events.body:
The trip was RydeTAXI, so the meter fare moves with distance and an unexplained longer route directly overcharges the rider [F6][RD-1][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists: 12:12–12:16, 2.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km [F3]. No incident on the replaced optimal stretch was recorded, only speed-band observations on Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 4) and Jurong Town Hall Road (band 5), which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on their own, so the RD-4(a) screen fails [F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

There is no rider consent for the 12:12 segment. The chat record is complete and contains no rider message at all, so nothing was sent before 12:12:15 agreeing to any route [F7]. The driver's statement that "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" was written after the trip and is a claim, not rider consent; it also places the driving on a rerouted path without naming any agreed road [F8][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply either: no rider-requested stop was measured on this segment, let alone one the rider named [F7][F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts as an unexcused deviation [RD-1].

No traffic incident qualifies, and no chat or phone-record evidence ties the driven path to any road the rider could have accepted, so the segment is neither exempt nor undetermined — it counts [F7][F8][F9][F11][RD-2][RD-5].

Amount: the fare record gives this trip's rate as distance fare ÷ distance = $15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.40968/km [F6]; the trace's stated rate is $1.4097/km, and using it 2.13 km × $1.4097/km = $3.0026, which rounds to $3.00 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The billed excess of $3.26 covers 2.31 km, including 0.18 km of corridor/matching slack that is not attributed to any segment and is not refunded under RD-2 [F4][F6][RD-2].

The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so this case makes the breach repeated and the account-review add-on applies alongside the refund [F14][RD-6]. The complaint and statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no safety escalation is required [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and found the route taken did not match the best route for your destination. One stretch of the trip added extra distance that was not explained or agreed with you, and your ride was charged by distance, so you paid more than you should have. We are sending you a $3.00 Ryde voucher for the extra distance. The voucher will be added to your Ryde account and applied automatically. No action is needed from you. The rest of your fare stands. Thank you for reporting this.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on one of your trips. The route taken included extra distance that was not agreed with the rider and was not explained by a traffic incident, so it counts as an unexcused detour. The rider is being given a $3.00 Ryde voucher for the extra distance, paid by Ryde, not deducted from you. Because this follows earlier upheld route disputes, your account is being sent for review. A reviewer will look at your recent route disputes and trips, then decide what happens next.

notices.text: We reviewed your trip and found the route taken did not match the best route for your destination. One stretch of the trip added extra distance that was not explained or agreed with you, and your ride was charged by distance, so you paid more than you should have. We are sending you a $3.00 Ryde voucher for the extra distance. The voucher will be added to your Ryde account and applied automatically. No action is needed from you. The rest of your fare stands. Thank you for reporting this.

We reviewed a route dispute on one of your trips. The route taken included extra distance that was not agreed with the rider and was not explained by a traffic incident, so it counts as an unexcused detour. The rider is being given a $3.00 Ryde voucher for the extra distance, paid by Ryde, not deducted from you. Because this follows earlier upheld route disputes, your account is being sent for review. A reviewer will look at your recent route disputes and trips, then decide what happens next.
